wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/obj/multiprop_parse.py: """`public $a, $b = 'x', $c = 0;` did not parse.

One property per declaration is not php's grammar, and the failure is not local: the parser gave up
at the comma and then met the class's closing brace at statement position, so ONE ordinary property
line turned into four errors and a refused program. Three of the auditors' programs are exactly
this — a stream wrapper declaring `public $context, $d = '…', $p = 0;`.

MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6, one program per case because a parse error inside `eval()` is a fatal
php does not let a caller catch:

    public $a, $b;                     accepted
